evidence: EXEC SQL via JC pre-SQL preprocessor (not native DB2/CICS)
CALL to MySQL_errno, MySQL_sqlstate, MySQL_error (GnuCOBOL MySQL C-library bindings)

purpose.summary: This program is a MySQL relational database handler (DAL – Data Access Layer) for an IRS (Internal Revenue/Reporting System) postings table within the ACAS (Applewood Computers Accounting System). It handles open, close, read-next, read-indexed, write, rewrite, delete, delete-all, and start operations against the IRSPOSTING-REC MySQL table, translating COBOL file-function codes into SQL commands via a JC pre-SQL preprocessor and direct MySQL C-library CALLs.

notable_features: EXEC SQL via JC pre-SQL preprocessor (inline SQL comments rather than true EXEC SQL blocks)
Direct CALL to MySQL C-library functions: MySQL_errno, MySQL_sqlstate, MySQL_error
BINARY-CHAR UNSIGNED and BINARY-LONG UNSIGNED GnuCOBOL data types
USAGE POINTER for MySQL result set handle
COPY statements for shared copybooks (mysql-variables.cpy, wsfnctn.cob, irswspost.cob, etc.)
SCREEN SECTION with foreground-color for error display
Cursor management via 88-level condition names (Cursor-Active / Cursor-Not-Active)
GO TO used extensively for function dispatch (EVALUATE ... GO TO pattern)
GNU GPL v2/v3 dual-licensed with commercial restriction notice
No COMP-3 usage despite accounting domain
verdict.notes: The file uses a JC pre-SQL preprocessor whose directives appear as COBOL comments (lines starting with *> /MYSQL ...\), so has_exec_sql in the mechanical indicators likely refers to these pseudo-SQL comment blocks rather than true EXEC SQL ... END-EXEC syntax. The program is part of a larger multi-module accounting system (ACAS v3.02+) with a clear versioning history and copyright lineage from 1976–2024, strongly indicating production-grade software. Author is Vincent B Coen of Applewood Computers.
